issues.body: The blurb says the tool proves a comparison about an integer "without disclosing it". In this same diff, COMMITTED_TERM_ANCHORS publishes only four value-to-anchor mappings, operand_enc is public, and the integration test requires that public disclosure; zk-tool.ts correctly states that a verifier holding the table can read off the committed value. Thus the prominent registry/palette copy makes an unqualified value-hiding claim that the shipped construction does not satisfy. The external-audit caveat does not cure this concrete disclosure contradiction.
issues.fix_hint: Replace the value-hiding claim with narrowly accurate copy, for example: "Prove a comparison about an integer using an in-tab UltraHonk proof; the public anchor identifies which of this build's four committed values was used. Research-grade; NOT externally audited." Keep the detailed panel disclosure text and add/adjust a metadata test that rejects a future "without disclosing the value" claim while the anchor table is enumerable.
issues.title: Tool blurb falsely claims the operand is not disclosed

verdict.summary: Round 4 finds a privacy-claim contradiction that the prior round missed. The implementation and detailed report correctly disclose that the public operand_enc is drawn from a four-entry published table and therefore identifies the value to a verifier holding the client code, but the eager tool metadata advertises proving about an integer "without disclosing it". That unqualified user-facing claim is not true for this shipped construction and violates the repository's ZK honesty posture. The real prove/verify/mutation integration test remains non-vacuous and CI-gated, and the detailed scope/replay/audit caveats are otherwise careful.
